entities.name: synaptic NMDAR activity in lamina II neurons

relationships.subject: spinal nerve ligation
relationships.evidence_quote: Quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis showed that compared with sham surgery, SNL caused a sustained reduction in Lrrc8a transcripts in the DRGs, but not the spinal cords, of rats at 5, 10, and 21 days after surgery (Fig. 2A).

relationships.subject: LRRC8A
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal injection of Lrrc8a-specific siRNA, but not control siRNA, for 6 consecutive days caused a gradual and profound reduction from baseline withdrawal thresholds in response to tactile, noxious pressure, and thermal stimuli (Fig. 3A), indicating the presence of allodynia and hyperalgesia.

relationships.subject: LRRC8A
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these findings demonstrate a direct association between LRRC8A and NMDAR proteins both in vivo and in vitro.

relationships.subject: LRRC8A
relationships.object: synaptic NMDAR activity in lamina II neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings collectively demonstrate that LRRC8A constitutively suppresses nociceptive hypersensitivity by interacting with and tonically inhibiting synaptic NMDARs in the spinal dorsal horn.

relationships.subject: LRRC8A
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these results support the notion that LRRC8A tonically suppresses NMDAR surface expression and their synaptic localization at spinal cord synapses.

relationships.subject: AP5
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal injection of (2R)-amino-5-phosphonopentanoate (AP5; 5 μg), a specific NMDAR antagonist, readily reversed the baseline withdrawal thresholds in rats treated with Lrrc8a-specific siRNA but had no effect in rats treated with control siRNA (Fig. 3B).

relationships.subject: LRR1 peptide
relationships.evidence_quote: Together, these results strongly suggest that LRRC8A physically interacts with NMDARs mainly through its LRR1 domain.

key_findings: Nerve injury reduced LRRC8A in the DRG; Lrrc8a knockdown, DRG-conditional knockout, or LRR-domain truncation (ebo/ebo) caused NMDAR-dependent pain hypersensitivity.
LRRC8A binds GluN1 via its C-terminal LRR1 domain and restrains synaptic NMDAR expression/activity in spinal dorsal horn; intrathecal Lrrc8a gene delivery reversed SNL-induced hypersensitivity.
